about: Round 2 of the port backlog slice src/ s-z and scripts/: the 146 rows of class workshop-tool that round 1 (move-rows/trillion-tools-m-z-scripts-parts.json, PR #122) left with no destination. The same source, keep, read_as_rows and provider detectors as round 1; the groups are round 1's groups that own one of those rows. A group whose imports all land now is moved by this row; a group still held is carried to its tool's from-old-trillion folder or retired, as the backlog row says.

groups.capability: build the interactive page that explains how Trillion is put together, from its explainer record
draw Trillion's app icon in every size from the supplied drawing, and the pictures shown when a story or the cover is shared or the app opens
turn the decision method's own sources into workflows that every account's AI can find and run when it designs a feature
photograph each what's-new tour live on a fresh account at the step that points at something, and keep the picture beside the tour
measure how well AI agents of each model use Trillion's tools on plain jobs, counting steps, errors and wrong changes, and print the table
let a tool's screen be its own code, built into a bundle the page loads when the screen opens, and list which built-in screens are still drawn by workspace code
turn a folder of agent skills into workflows every account's AI can find, read and run
start a community from its configuration file and hand it over to the person who will run it with a one-time link
load the shared tool rows and tool folders at deploy and take each container tool's files from its folder instead of typing them into the row
close a list row when I say in my own message that I already did the thing, but only when the answer is a clear yes
draft and send a sales contract to a customer from my own offers, prices and customers, and set things up once the deal is sent
keep links I saved elsewhere, such as a browser's pinned tabs and folders and a service's bookmarks, so every AI and screen can read them
keep my own logins sealed so I can always see and copy them, let my AIs read only the ones I allow, and never show a value I kept private
show my screens from a catalogue of reads and layouts, page by page, each drawn from the facts its reads answered
keep my search index beside a copy of my results, fed by small pages of what changed, so my saves never wait on it
find anything from one box: jump to a screen, a calendar event, an AI, an action or a search hit across what I said, saw, named and noted
sell one purchase that pays for several people, with each offer naming its seats and a buyer picking how many
send one message to all of my AIs at once, kept word for word in the shared conversation
let Trillion's own code act for an account when no person is signed in, with a short-lived proof only the account's own policy can make
run Trillion's own capability checks, each on its own schedule, and show their results as rows only in the operating account
tell the person of an account something from the service itself, such as a bill notice or a spending alert
run the service's own price experiments, each kept in its own book and read by what each published
publish price guidance as editable rows, while the offer owner still sets the real prices
publish the operator's shared records, such as show rules, setup context, releases and brand, to every region, and make them current right after a deploy
keep the service's own signing secrets and sign-in app values sealed in a locked box, and change the master keys without ever reading one back
watch the service itself, such as the share of calls each store failed and whether what landed on main went live, on its own schedule
keep each account's setup access request in a book of its own, so preparing and fulfilling it reaches only that request
let a person ask for the Trillion app to be installed on a device and follow the provider's delivery until setup is truly finished
show each setup step with the real things found behind it, such as which AIs, devices and sources, and what Trillion did this past week
walk a new person through first setup: the apps to install on their devices, the AIs to connect, and one saved run that resumes where they stopped
show a big shared collection of files page by page as cards with small cover pictures and the files each record points to
choose where shares from the phone, browser and Android go, which AI action each site starts, and look back at what was shared before
keep anything sent to Trillion, a link, file or words, safely at the edge when the person's store is busy, then deliver it with its status
open a share link on my own web address instead of Trillion's, once I own the address
run each command in a shared space exactly once: remember what it did, ask again when unsure, and keep it from half finishing
keep a shared space's posts, files and tasks in separate stores so a busy space never slows another, and read them back merged in order
publish the tools a space shares as public pages and keep their use counts
publish my progress as a public page with a picture card and a link that credits me for each person who joins through it
give every account ready made workflows and defaults, and keep only the changes the person makes to them
let a visitor try Trillion's own workspace live in a throwaway account that empties itself when its time ends
host a site's own backend inside Trillion: install its code, give it a private database and serve its files
read public repositories of agent skills and offer each skill as a Marketplace workflow
receive a text message sent to the AI's phone number and hand it to the person's AIs
draft, approve and publish my social posts now or at a set time, and read back where each went
connect the original repository behind an app, edit its source with revision checks and preview the rebuilt app
give shared tasks to people and AIs, keep an order and dependencies between them, and cap how many one AI works at once
list the AIs in a shared space for its members, and hand an AI working there what members said most recently
move a shared space's content into its own store and clear the old copy only after the new one reads back exactly
keep a shared board's cards consistent when several people edit at once, even when the board is split across stores
count how much each member has written in a community and show it beside their name
invite people to a space by link, email address or phone number and show the invitation in every state it can be in
decide who may do what in a space by each member's kind and the space's own rules, and open or close a space to everyone
name a space by its name when posting to it, find items in it by their words and pick things of mine to share into it
give an AI the tools to read and change a pursuit's people, shared things, rules and agents
estimate what a person's services cost from measured use and listed rates, warn at a budget and stop paid work
send each action on a shared space to the place that holds it, whether from a page, a tool or an AI
start a new account with the rules and catalog items Trillion does for everyone until the person changes them
keep the shared tool rows a deploy ships in the worker's key-value storage, splitting large values into checked parts that are read back whole
turn a finished decision into an anonymous public story of what was weighed, what was chosen and how it turned out, and keep or take it down
decide which subscription and billing profile a purchase belongs to, so a usage meter is never counted twice for the same customer
let an AI or a rule suggest tasks found in a meeting or an email, which the person reviews and accepts before they become real tasks
tell one person something through every way they chose to hear that kind of news, and stop when the thing it was about is settled
keep the tables that record how tools are used, the same for the shared pool and for every owner that keeps its own
list and run Trillion's tools for any AI app over the standard tool protocol, locally or on the hosted web address
let an AI write a guided tour for the moment the person is in, file it in a category and show it on their open page at once
make a cover picture for each saved video, catching up on older files newest first without restarting when new ones keep arriving
let someone look at my Trillion read only for a few days, exactly as I see it, with every change refused
show a visitor who is not signed in the same price every time, and keep that price once they sign in
turn any recording already in the person's files into a voice memo with its words kept beside it and handed to their AIs
stop a reminder about a waiting or held thing once that thing is no longer waiting
send work, tasks, tours and instructions from Trillion to customers' AIs, to one person, a group, a test group or everyone, in a time window
send a saved edit from the media editor to my own video editor and attach the video I exported there
keep the media editor's open session, its published versions and its track check on the person's own store
show the media library and search what was said or seen in recordings, and change the next-edit suggestion
show the signed-in person's message inbox and tell the sender whether the AI can be reached or will find the message later
show the posts and the posting calendar on the signed-in page, the same posts their AIs list and change
show my automations on the signed-in page: what sets each off and what it does, and draw a workflow or one run as a board of steps
write a job done in several steps, have my AI, agents and tools answer each step, and keep every answer
write a Workshop task's history to a file and read it back whole, even a row too big for the file limit, in exact byte pieces
keep each Workshop task whole and a small index of every task for fast questions across all of them
list the signed-in page's current script, stylesheet and screen files by their content names, kept by a browser for a year
keep the serving Worker's content-named workspace pieces so a page that is loading never meets a missing file

not_provider_calls.why: placeCacheFolder(env = process.env) reads the cache folder a computer names in its process environment; it is no Worker binding.
